items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Judy Williams in his response; he only discusses Lips Fades and Benny Moulton's Blue Devils.

ctx.x: Tonation is that that you get out of the horns. Like some fellas say, well man his tone sounds like a pea shooter. Another guy says he has a tone bigger round as an apple. Well here's what that means. If a guy plays a horn and he has a light sound coming out, well that's a pea shooter sound. You know you play your own sound like, Alright then if he hears a great big sound like, Look, you say that's a sound as big around as a bowl. Because it's beautiful. It has a space that it's covered. And a pea shooter doesn't…
Well now you're talking about blues and Judy Williams and all that. Did you know Lips Fades when you were in fact?

Lips and I played together. Lips came to Dallas, Texas in 1926 with Benny Moulton's Blue Devils. And Basie was the pianist in this band. And Oren Page was the bass. So they thought that Lips Page and Oren and the Brothers weren't even related. And Page and I, we used to go out at night and sit out and play with each other. And Compton with John on the piano.
